$comment: compare_labels gold set. Every anchor is a phrase that must (or must not) appear, after whitespace/case/quote normalisation, in the section compare_labels returns for that side. status: draft = written from the article/label knowledge but NOT yet checked against the live label by a human; verified = checked live on verified_on by verified_by. Only verified cases can fail the CI gate. Freeze by verifying, never by editing an anchor to make it pass. Sources: 'One molecule, two labels' (pharmatools.ai/us-uk-labelling, 25 Aug 2026) for the first four drugs. Run 1 (14 Sep 2026) showed two engine limits worth keeping visible: (a) every section is cut at 1,400 chars, so anchors past the cut are reported UNVERIFIABLE; (b) eMC/openFDA best-match sometimes picks OTC or combination products or nothing — cases note what each side resolved to. Product names are used where the generic resolved badly. Cases may carry us_drug / uk_drug (passed through to compare_labels' per-side names) when one string cannot name both products (Farxiga/Forxiga, Prilosec/Losec).

cases.divergence: US indicates for MACE and renal risk reduction; UK 4.1 lists glycaemic control only and cross-references the outcome data.

US contraindicates personal/family history of MTC or MEN 2; UK 4.3 is hypersensitivity only. Run 2 (dump): the US section uses the abbreviations 'MTC' and 'MEN 2'; the expansion is in 5.1. Anchor corrected to the label's wording — the claim is unchanged.
US: prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma (monotherapy). UK: add-on therapy only, in patients inadequately controlled on inhaled corticosteroids.

must_contain: prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma

cases.divergence: Both mention neuropsychiatric events, but only the US carries a boxed warning (a separate LOINC section, outside this mapping). This case checks the mapped Warnings sections both surface the risk — a convergence case. Run 1: anchor(s) missing from a section the engine cut at 1,400 chars — reported UNVERIFIABLE, not a miss. Fix belongs in @pharmatools/drug-data (expose the cap), not in this anchor.

UK 4.3 makes the Pregnancy Prevention Programme itself a contraindication and adds hepatic insufficiency, hyperlipidaemia, hypervitaminosis A and concomitant tetracyclines; US lists pregnancy and hypersensitivity only.

Both restrict post-tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy use in children, but the UK 4.3 also contraindicates known CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolisers and breastfeeding, which the US keeps in warnings. Verify which codeine product each source resolves to before freezing. Run 1: passed, but resolved to combination products on both sides (US acetaminophen+codeine, UK Boots ibuprofen+codeine) — the anchors held because the paediatric restrictions are class-wide. Decide whether a plain-codeine product should be pinned instead.
Same use, different spelling — a retrieval sanity check: US 'hyperlipidemia', UK 'hypercholesterolaemia'.

UK 4.4 carries the statin-class interstitial lung disease warning; US Warnings and Precautions does not. Run 1: anchor(s) missing from a section the engine cut at 1,400 chars — reported UNVERIFIABLE, not a miss. Fix belongs in @pharmatools/drug-data (expose the cap), not in this anchor.

Both contraindicate metabolic acidosis; the UK 4.3 also contraindicates acute alcohol intoxication/alcoholism, which the US keeps in warnings. Run 1: the generic 'metformin' resolved the UK side to Alogliptin/Metformin (a combination); switched to Glucophage so both sides are the plain product. Run 2: 'Glucophage' found nothing on openFDA; US back to the generic name (run 1 resolved it), UK pinned to Glucophage.

US contraindicates use in the setting of CABG surgery (absent from UK 4.3); UK contraindicates the third trimester of pregnancy (US handles pregnancy in warnings). Run 1: US side unavailable (openFDA best-match failed on 'ibuprofen') and the UK side resolved to a Boots paediatric OTC suspension whose 4.3 wording differs. Kept as an engine-resolution finding; verify before changing the product name. Run 2 (dump): the UK 4.3 says 'Last trimester of pregnancy'; anchor corrected to the label's wording. US pinned to Motrin for the same openFDA recency reason; may still resolve to an OTC label — verify. Run 3: US side still unavailable by brand (Motrin / Prilosec) — openFDA's five most recently updated labels for these names are OTC and carry no contraindications section, so the engine returns null. Kept as an engine-resolution finding.

UK 4.3 spells out cross-reactivity with cephalosporins, carbapenems and monobactams; US refers to beta-lactams generally. Run 3 (dump): the UK 4.3 writes 'betalactam' as one word; anchor moved to the class names it spells out (penicillins, carbapenem, monobactam), which is the divergence the case is about.
Spelling: US 'nonvalvular atrial fibrillation', UK 'non-valvular atrial fibrillation'. Note norm() folds dashes but not the missing hyphen, so both anchors are genuinely side-specific.
UK 4.3 contraindicates hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk; US lists active pathological bleeding and severe hypersensitivity only.

UK 4.3 is a long list (inability to have regular blood tests, prior drug-induced agranulocytosis, paralytic ileus, uncontrolled epilepsy, active liver disease); US contraindications are hypersensitivity only, with the haematological controls in the REMS/warnings. Run 1: 'clozapine' resolved US to Versacloz and found nothing on the eMC; switched to Clozaril, licensed under that name in both markets.

Both contraindicate angioedema history and aliskiren co-use in diabetes; the UK 4.3 also contraindicates the second and third trimesters of pregnancy, which the US carries as a boxed warning, not a contraindication.

UK 4.3 contraindicates evidence or history of thyroid dysfunction and pregnancy/lactation; US contraindications are cardiac (cardiogenic shock, sick sinus syndrome, AV block) and hypersensitivity, with thyroid in warnings. Run 1: UK side unavailable — the eMC search for 'amiodarone' returned no usable product. Kept as an engine-resolution finding; verify what the eMC lists before choosing a product name.

UK 4.3 contraindicates co-administration with nelfinavir; US contraindicates rilpivirine-containing products and keeps nelfinavir in interactions. Run 1: US side unavailable — openFDA best-match failed on 'omeprazole' (many OTC labels). Kept as an engine-resolution finding. Run 2: both sides failed on the generic (openFDA returns the five most recently updated labels, which for omeprazole are OTC and have no contraindications section). Pinned to Prilosec / Losec. Run 3: US side still unavailable by brand (Motrin / Prilosec) — openFDA's five most recently updated labels for these names are OTC and carry no contraindications section, so the engine returns null. Kept as an engine-resolution finding.

US carries the tissue-agnostic TMB-H (tumour mutational burden-high) indication; the UK/EU SmPC does not. Also a spelling check: 'tumor' vs 'tumour'. Run 1: anchor(s) missing from a section the engine cut at 1,400 chars — reported UNVERIFIABLE, not a miss. Fix belongs in @pharmatools/drug-data (expose the cap), not in this anchor.

US indications include ductal carcinoma in situ and risk reduction in high-risk women; UK 4.1 is breast cancer treatment (some UK products also list anovulatory infertility). Run 1: anchor(s) missing from a section the engine cut at 1,400 chars — reported UNVERIFIABLE, not a miss. Fix belongs in @pharmatools/drug-data (expose the cap), not in this anchor.

Convergence case: both markets now indicate for type 2 diabetes, heart failure and chronic kidney disease. Guards against false divergence. Run 1: anchor(s) missing from a section the engine cut at 1,400 chars — reported UNVERIFIABLE, not a miss. Fix belongs in @pharmatools/drug-data (expose the cap), not in this anchor. Run 2 (dump): the generic 'dapagliflozin' resolved the US side to a generic manufacturer's label, which can carve out patent-protected indications, and was cut at the cap. Pinned to the reference products (Farxiga US / Forxiga UK) via the new per-side names.

UK 4.3 contraindicates use in women of childbearing potential unless the Pregnancy Prevention Programme conditions are met; US contraindications cover urea cycle disorders, POLG mitochondrial disease and migraine prophylaxis in pregnancy, without a PPP. Verify which products each source resolves to.
Status semantics, not content: 'acetaminophen' is the US generic; the eMC lists paracetamol. compare_labels must report the UK side as unavailable with an explanatory note rather than a bare null.
Mirror of the above: openFDA has no 'paracetamol' generic; the UK side should be ok and the US side unavailable.

cases.verified_by: construction — no such product can exist in either source
cases.divergence: Neither source can return a label; the tool must return a single explanatory error naming resolve_drug_name, not a comparison of nulls.
